text:
laura: Heads up — finance flagged an unexpected 429 blast from Dedicated last night. They say the tenant was doing regular heartbeat jobs but still hit limits. Looks like we're mixing RPM/TPM + concurrency checks and it's getting confusing for customers. any thoughts?
sam: Which layer returned the 429 (edge/router/scheduler)? Can you paste the headers or a log snippet?
laura: Edge 429s. Headers showed `X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 34`. Log: `org=acme-prod, burst_credits=0, in_flight=12, concurrency_limit=10`
miguel: That log explains it — we currently accept based on token bucket then let concurrency enforcement happen later. Race: accept path drains bursts and later scheduler rejects because concurrency exceeded. We need atomicity.
ravi: Proposal: require both token and concurrency checks at the router before accepting. If concurrency full, either reject or queue for a short tick (<=50ms) to reduce tail rejections.
sam: Queueing at router risks puffing p99 latency. Alternative: accept at router only if both pass, otherwise return 429 with `retry-after`. Let scheduler not have to drop accepted requests.
laura: Customers prefer a clear 429 than a later 5xx or partial success. Prefer upstream rejection with deterministic headers.
miguel: If we go upstream-reject, we should fix the burst logic: token bucket and concurrency need to be consistent in fast paths. Maybe introduce an atomic CAS in the edge state or move to centralized lease service for short window.
ravi: Also add `retry-after` and include token state in 429 body (`burst_remaining`, `tokens_remaining`, `concurrency_limit`) so smart clients can backoff correctly.
laura: Good call. UX-wise, console should show burst credits + estimated refill for the org so support can explain. Right now the console just shows RPM usage which is misleading.
sam: Another idea: add a tiny edge smoothing leaky bucket per org that can absorb brief spikes (1-2s) instead of hitting Dedicated pools. Memory cost small and helps noisy heartbeats.
miguel: Fine, but document it — smoothing changes traffic shape for perf tests and billing. Emit metrics marking smoothed requests vs direct passthrough.
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-215 — tagged eng-platform and paging oncall.
sam: I'll spin up a PoC for edge smoothing this week. It's small: a per-org ring + leaky counter.
laura: Action items: I will draft RFC for "atomic rate accept" + policy doc on concurrency vs tokens. sam: edge PoC. miguel: change accept path to be atomic or add centralized lease. ravi: telemetry schema for detailed rejection reasons and burst metrics. Assigning owners in-thread. :raised_hands:
miguel: Also suggest default plan-level concurrency caps and console override per-org (audit log). Saves us from one-off escalations.
ravi: Telemetry list: `rate.accepted`, `rate.rejected.concurrency`, `rate.rejected.tokens`, `burst.refill_seconds`, `smoothed.count` — emit per-org and per-region. This will help billing and alerts.
sam: Sounds good. I'll update the edge PoC PR with metrics hooks.
laura: Thanks all — RFC incoming. Will tag infra and docs when drafted.
